# Revise

Read when `dt status --skill architecture-design` reports Revise: a technical change with no spec change, or probe results to fold in. It ends at the Review Gate in `../SKILL.md`, following `writing-rules.md`. Example: `examples-revise.md`.

1. Write a new decision whose Context explains what was learned ("the simulator is 40× too slow for QR-02 at 1M steps"). Then supersede the old decision if the new one reverses it, or revise it in place if the new one changes only part of it (`decisions.md`).
2. Update every section and contract the change touches (tech stack, components, Overview; contracts per `contracts.md`), and run the Review Gate.
3. If a contract changes, list its consumers (its **Used by**): their pipelines and tasks need revisiting. Record the pipelines' share for `pipeline-design`: `dt route pipeline-design "<change> (PL-02, PL-03)" --from architecture-design`. A frozen interface's type, samples and fake change with it, in a new interface task Replan adds (a `contract-change` edge).

## Probe results

For each probe in `probes_answered` or `probes_failed`, read its entry with `dt section PB-NN` (its Verdict, each check's Result, its Caveats), never `probes/`. Then, for each decision it informs:

| Result | Change |
|---|---|
| Every check passed | Cite the finding in the decision's Context ("PB-01, 2026-10-20: 6 of 6 institutions link; history 13–24 months") and delete its Risks line. It becomes Accepted at approval |
| Waived | Cite the waiver and the user's reason in Context; keep the Risks line. It becomes Accepted at approval |
| A check failed, and another option still meets the requirements | Steps 1–3: revise the decision in place, or supersede it |
| A check failed, and no affordable option meets a requirement | Name the requirement and the finding at the gate. Only the user can change it, through `spec-writing` |
| Observed fields differ from a contract type | The type's fields and invariants follow the evidence ("`merchant_entity_id` is None on 38% of rows"); its **Cases** may name the probe's samples (`contracts.md`) |

### AD-03: Sharadar for prices, corporate actions, membership and identity
**Status:** Proposed · **Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Scope:** `data`
- **Context:** DATA-01–DATA-04 and UNIV-01–UNIV-03 need delisted stocks, membership with effective dates for ≥15 years, splits, dividends, spin-offs, ticker changes and delistings, and a permanent identifier; QR-01 caps extra spend at $50/month and the brief has a Sharadar subscription. Sharadar's [prices page](https://sharadar.com/prices) (read 2026-10-17) states SEP covers active and delisted US stocks with history to December 1997, an `sp500` table with "additions and deletions with effective dates" from January 1998, an `actions` table of splits, dividends, spin-offs, ticker changes and delisting details, `close` split-adjusted, `closeadj` adjusted for splits, dividends and spin-offs, and daily updates. The [fundamentals page](https://sharadar.com/fundamentals) (read 2026-10-17) states TICKERS has a permanent `permaticker` key and ACTIONS covers listing and delisting dates, delist reasons and acquisition counterparties. Neither page says whether delisting payouts carry a value, whether TICKERS keeps sector history, or how revisions show in `lastupdated`.
- **Decision:** Sharadar SEP (OHLCV, `closeunadj`), ACTIONS, TICKERS and SP500 through the Nasdaq Data Link tables API, behind the `data` `Source` protocol. `StockId` is the `permaticker`; each share class has its own (UNIV-03). Full downloads use the bulk export; updates filter on `lastupdated` (INGST-02).
- **Alternatives:** CRSP via WRDS — the reference standard for delisting returns, but needs an institutional licence. Norgate Data — has historical S&P membership and delisted stocks, but a second paid subscription close to the cap and Windows-centred tooling. Free scraped constituents (Wikipedia, EODHD free tier) — accurate only back to about 2000 per those sources, and no delisted prices.
- **Consequences:** History starts 1998, so DATA-01's 15 years holds with ~13 to spare. The adapter is the only Sharadar-aware code; a switch touches `data.vendors` only. Delisting returns depend on what ACTIONS records (AD-08).
- **Probe:** PB-01 — on the user's subscription: do SEP/ACTIONS/SP500/TICKERS return delisted members back to 1998; do ACTIONS delisting and acquisition rows carry a payout value; does TICKERS keep sector history; do `lastupdated` filters return revisions; and how long does a bulk export take?

<!-- docs/architecture.md:174 -->
### AD-05: Point-in-time sectors from SEC EDGAR SIC codes
**Status:** Proposed · **Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Scope:** `data`
- **Context:** DATA-07 and FCST-03 need each stock's sector on each date. Sharadar's [fundamentals page](https://sharadar.com/fundamentals) (read 2026-10-17) lists sector, industry, SIC sector, SIC industry and Fama industry fields on TICKERS but says nothing about history, so it may be the current value only. The SEC's company filing metadata records an SIC code with each filer, and is free (QR-01).
- **Decision:** If PB-01 shows TICKERS keeps dated classifications, use them. Otherwise build sector intervals from the SIC code recorded on each company's EDGAR filings, mapped to SIC divisions, linked to `StockId` by the CIK on TICKERS; a stock's first known sector is backfilled to its first membership date and flagged `assumed`.
- **Alternatives:** GICS history from S&P — licensed, beyond the budget. Current Sharadar sector for all dates — fails DATA-07's reclassification check.
- **Consequences:** SIC divisions are coarser than GICS sectors (10 vs 11, different boundaries); only FCST-03 uses sectors, as a fixed attribute.
- **Probe:** PB-02 — does EDGAR expose a per-filing SIC history for delisted S&P 500 members since 1998, and can every member be linked by CIK?

<!-- docs/architecture.md:196 -->
### AD-08: Returns built from unadjusted prices, actions and the exchange calendar
**Status:** Proposed · **Date:** 2026-10-17 · **Scope:** `data`
- **Context:** VALID-05 needs adjusted returns equal to economic total return within 0.01 pp; PANEL-03 needs delisting returns (cash payout, or −100% flagged estimated); PANEL-04 forbids filled gaps; DATA-05 and VALID-03 need the exchange calendar. RF-03 counts horizons in rows, which spec FCST-01 forbids. Test planning (2026-10-17, TC-02, TC-03, TC-05) found two cells unspecified: the return on the first session after a missing bar, and which session carries the delisting return when the index removal takes effect that same session.
- **Decision:** Daily total return = (unadjusted close × split factor + cash dividend) / previous unadjusted close − 1, with spin-offs taken from Sharadar's `closeadj` ratio on the ex-date; VALID-05 cross-checks every action day against `closeadj`. Delisting return: the recorded payout or final price versus the last close; with neither, −100% and `estimated=True`. Trading days come from `exchange_calendars` XNYS; a date where SEP has bars for most members but XNYS says closed (or the reverse) fails validation.
  - *Gaps:* sessions with no bar stay NaN (PANEL-04). The first session with a bar after a gap carries the multi-session total return from the last close before the gap, with the split factors and cash dividends whose ex-dates fall in the gap or on that session, so a holder's price move over the gap isn't lost.
  - *Delisting session:* the delisting return sits on the first XNYS session after the stock's last bar, the session a holder at the last close is paid on. It is carried only when the stock was a member on its last bar's session, and it is the one return allowed where `member` is False: `member` keeps following the index (the removal takes effect that session, as `membership_as_of` reports), so a position held at the last close still earns the payout or the −100%. Every later cell is NaN.
- **Alternatives:** Use `closeadj` returns directly — no independent check of VALID-05 and no delisting payouts. A hand-maintained holiday list — error-prone for special closures. NaN on the first session after a gap — loses the price move a holder had over the gap. The delisting return folded into the last bar's session, or `member` set True on the removal session — misdates the payout, or makes the panel disagree with `membership_as_of`.
- **Consequences:** Every return in the platform comes from `data.returns_panel`; horizons everywhere count XNYS sessions (AD-15). A cell after a gap spans several sessions, so a per-session statistic (volatility, covariance) sees one larger move rather than missing days; gaps are rare and VALID-03 reports each one. Consumers apply a session's return to the positions held at the previous close, not to that session's `member` mask, or they drop every delisting return.
- **Probe:** PB-01 — whether ACTIONS gives payouts determines how many delisting returns are `estimated`.

steps.text:
I've written AD-03, AD-05 and AD-08 up for the waiver. They're ready for your approval. Nothing about how the design works has changed: only Context and Risks now record that the probes were waived and why.

**Files:** `docs/architecture.md`, now `Draft` (dated 2026-10-18). `docs/probes.md` has both probes set to `Waived · 2026-10-18 — I'll rerun them later from another network`. Both files are uncommitted.

**What changed:**

| | Change |
|---|---|
| **AD-03** (Sharadar) | Context says PB-01 was waived with no checks run, because the access step was blocked on the network path. Payout values, sector history and revisions stay unknown, and the build uses the synthetic source (AD-22) until PB-01 runs. |
| **AD-05** (sectors) | Context says both probes were waived. Until PB-01 shows dated sectors on TICKERS, the build uses the EDGAR path. Whether EDGAR keeps a dated SIC history is still unconfirmed. |
| **AD-08** (returns) | Context says PB-01 was waived, so we don't yet know how many delisting returns will be estimated at −100%. |
| **Risks** | All three PB-related lines are kept, each marked "waived 2026-10-18, rerun later". QR-03's bulk-export time is marked unmeasured. |
| **Changelog** | One new row for this change. |

The shape stays at six packages, as you said. Every requirement is still covered, no decision contradicts another, and no contract changed, so nothing needs routing to pipeline-design.

**Lint:** `dt lint docs/` reports 9 errors and 4 warnings, exactly the same as before this edit. None are in this edit:
- Nine `app/pipelines.md` steps (PL-36–PL-43) whose outputs don't name a contract type. That file belongs to pipeline-design.
- The `data` contract is 215 lines, over its 200-line limit.
- The roadmap names skills that aren't installed (`dataviz`, `api-probe`).

The "roadmap stale" flag only appears because the architecture is in Draft while you review it. It clears when you approve.

## ASSUMPTIONS
- AD-05 isn't rewritten. The build just uses its EDGAR branch, which `EdgarSicSource` in the `data` pipelines already implements.
- After approval, AD-03, AD-05 and AD-08 become **Accepted** because the probes are waived, and their Risks lines stay. When you rerun the probes, any failure comes back here as a Revise.

## Open questions
- Should the 9 existing lint errors in `app/pipelines.md` go to pipeline-design before build-planning? I'd do that next, because build-planning will probably refuse to plan while lint has errors.

Do you approve this revision?
